questions: Did s-bend progress rise above 0.158 and slalom progress above 0.1075 compared with iteration 8?
Did max_error stay at or below 0.069 on every track? If it rose, at what progress does the robot leave the track?
Did steering_oscillation or control_effort rise sharply with the higher ground speed, which would point to the controller gain being too high at this speed?
Did any run finish, and if so, what is the completion_time?

intent: Keep the iteration 8 best state and take one bounded speed step, wheel_radius 0.04 to 0.044 m, to find whether speed still raises s-bend and slalom progress with max_error at or below 0.069. Hold the sensor layout (x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m, 12 mm footprint), body, track 0.12 m and mass 0.6 kg fixed so the result is attributable to wheel radius alone. Fall back to 0.04 m if progress is flat or max_error exceeds 0.069.
learning: Wheel radius 0.03 to 0.04 m has raised progress in small steps (s-bend 0.149 to 0.155 to 0.158) with max_error held. If the 0.044 m step gives a flat or worse result, speed is at its useful limit and the final geometry should be wheel_radius 0.04 m. The remaining gains are likely in the controller, which the Integrator should tune for the faster robot.
rationale: Iteration 8 (wheel_radius 0.04 m, all else as iteration 5) scored 51.13, the best so far. Progress rose on the s-bend (0.155 to 0.158) and slalom (0.1066 to 0.1075), and max_error stayed at or below 0.069 on every track (oval 0.0608, s-bend 0.0684, slalom 0.0634). The Integrator's rule for this case is that speed is still helping, so wheel_radius 0.04 m is kept. The oval score fell because of the finish-free scoring of progress, but progress there was unchanged at 0.1075. The gain is small: about +0.003 progress per 0.005 m of wheel radius, and max_error on the s-bend is now close to the 0.069 band. Iterations 0 to 7 showed that sensor span, footprint, lead, body, track, mass and controller gains barely move max_error, and that track (0.10 and 0.14 m) and mass (0.5 kg) changes lowered progress. Speed is the only lever that has raised progress without pushing drift past the band. I take one bounded step to wheel_radius 0.044 m, with mass 0.6 kg, track 0.12 m and the same sensor layout. I expect s-bend progress to rise to about 0.16 and slalom to about 0.108, with s-bend max_error at or below 0.069. If max_error goes above 0.069 or progress is flat, I will return wheel_radius to 0.04 m (the iteration 8 best) and stop changing geometry, since the remaining limit is the controller's response at speed.
